R3.text: single entity: Spring Data JPA returns null when a query method declared with a single entity (not Optional, not a collection) finds no row -- a @Query, a derived query or findById on the repository -- and raises IncorrectResultSizeDataAccessException for more than one. JPA's TypedQuery.getSingleResult() throws NoResultException for no row, which answers 500 where the source answered its own null path (typically 404). Port the member as query.getResultStream().findFirst().orElse(null) when the source guarantees at most one row (an id or unique key), or catch NoResultException and return null; never getSingleResult() bare, and never turn the source's null into an exception or an empty object. optional: an Optional return is Optional.empty() for no row (getResultStream().findFirst()). collection: a collection return is an empty collection for no row (getResultList()).

R4.action: change that parameter to Set<? extends ConstraintViolation<?>> (jakarta.validation.ConstraintViolation) and have the handler pass the set validator.validate(<body>) returned; where the helper walked bindingResult.getFieldErrors(), iterate the violations and read each FieldError accessor from its ConstraintViolation equivalent (FieldError.getField() -> violation.getPropertyPath().toString(), getDefaultMessage() -> getMessage(), getRejectedValue() -> getInvalidValue(), getObjectName() -> java.beans.Introspector.decapitalize(violation.getRootBeanClass().getSimpleName())); keep the helper's output (the header or body it renders) exactly as it was
R4.object_name: getObjectName() is the BINDING name Spring gave the validated @RequestBody, not the class name: RequestResponseBodyMethodProcessor binds it under Conventions.getVariableNameForParameter, which for a non-collection, non-array type is ClassUtils.getShortNameAsProperty = java.beans.Introspector.decapitalize(<short name>) (OwnerDto -> ownerDto, URLDto -> URLDto). A body declared as a collection or array is named differently (Conventions pluralizes, e.g. ownerDtoList): that shape is unresolved here and the source capture's errors header decides. Checked by validation-object-name.test.py (Spring's own ClassUtils against this expression) and by M4 parity on the errors header (M-3 2026-09-30: the v28 candidate rendered OwnerDto where the source sent ownerDto)
